items.title: An interval exchange transformation all of whose connection times are finite is periodic
items.author: Przemyslaw Berk; Frank Trujillo
items.work: Ergodic properties of infinite extension of symmetric interval exchange transformations
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 191-193: if for every subinterval except one the connection time is finite, then the interval exchange transformation has only periodic orbits, with a finite decomposition into periodic components on which the period is uniform. The proof (source lines 195-211) uses three ingredients that the statement does not mention: the orbit set of the discontinuities is finite under the hypothesis, so it generates a finite partition; every iterate acts continuously on each element of that partition, because a discontinuity of an iterate would have to be an image of a partition point; and Poincare recurrence supplies a return time whose return is exact, the two other possibilities being excluded by the choice of the partition. Only then does the argument conclude that a power of the transformation fixes an element on which it is a piecewise translation.

proof_spans.label: the complete author proof of the labelled lemma, retained line for line
